g.title: egress_policy
g.text: What the forward chain decides, in order

g.title: node1
g.text: 1 · ip daddr in the node's own space
+ every address the node answers on

g.title: agent
g.text: an agent's packet: only the egress proxy
stands in for what it may reach

g.title: open
g.text: what the machine already had open

g.title: held
g.text: a machine taken back from the last runner,
until its record says what it carries

g.title: allowed
g.text: machine . destination, with a counter, 6 h

g.title: tagD
g.text: and nothing else, when the tag says so

g.title: dflt
g.text: the default: open beyond the node

g.title: home
g.text: the way back, and only for a connection

g.title: lat
g.text: one machine to another, said out loud

g.title: note
g.text: 1 is first because 4 is what would otherwise carry it: the
node's LAN is reached through the uplink like everything else,
so a drop written after the accept never runs. It matches the
destination alone and not the pair of interfaces - what is kept
away is a place, not a path, and a rule naming wan0 would stop
applying the day there is a second way out.
2 and 3 are between them, so a tag cannot open the node and a
tag that closes a machine is reached by what its own rules did
1c is after 1b, so a runner's restart cuts nothing a machine
had open, and before 4, which a machine in no tag set reaches.
4 is open on purpose. There is no allowlist to write yet, so
the accept records where it went instead - see @observed, and
